conviction_note: The two big customers and the closest peer point to a Q3 revenue print in the upper half of the $315-345m guide, against a $330m consensus. But in October semicap stocks sold off on record prints (Lam -11.8%, UCT -9% on Oct 30). The Q4 guide has to clear about $355m to honour the company's own FY >=30% commitment, while Lam guided its December quarter only +4.6% q/q and flagged component constraints. So p_up is 54 on a 16% absolute move. The finding sum (+1.5) and the scaled number (+1.3) agree in sign and size.
bar: Q3 revenue $330.2m and non-GAAP EPS $0.45 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-10-26, whisper also $0.45: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ICHR/21402). Benzinga lists $330.1m / $0.43 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ICHR/earnings-forecasts), so two sources agree on revenue. Company guide: $315-345m, non-GAAP EPS $0.40-0.50, GM 14.5-15.5% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652535/000165253526000066/ex-991_26q2xearnings.htm; GM guide per https://quartr.com/events/ichor-holdings-ltd-ichr-q2-2026_ofpg9YHu). Implied Q4 bar: FY2025 revenue was $947.7m and H1 2026 about $551m (Q1 ~$256m + Q2 $294.8m). Management's 'FY growth >=30%' and 'H2 >=25% above H1' then require Q4 of about $351-358m if Q3 lands at $330m. Any Q4 guide midpoint below about $355m breaks the company's own stated commitment.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/ichr/short-interest): 2,662,218 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 7.1% of 37.45m shares outstanding, 3.49 days to cover. That is down from 3,174,189 (8.5%, 4.22 days) on 2026-09-30 and up from 1.69m (4.5%) at the end of July: elevated but not crowded. Skew_25d is +1.09 vol points (balanced) and the put/call OI ratio is 0.73. The event-implied move is 13.6%, against a median absolute reaction of 18.8% over the last eight prints. The stock is -39.5% over 20 days and -65.9% from its 52-week high, after a $195m ATM sold at an average $80.70 in Q2. Earnings Whispers bullish sentiment fell to 10.5% from 28.4%.

findings.finding: Lam Research, roughly half of Ichor's revenue (51-56% in every 10-K from FY2016 to FY2021; Lam plus Applied was 76% in FY2025), grew revenue 22% q/q in its September 2026 quarter ($6.72bn to $8.22bn). That beat its own $8.10bn guide midpoint, against Ichor's guided +12% q/q midpoint ($294.8m to $330m) and a $330.2m consensus. Lam's quarter ended Sep 27 and Ichor's about Sep 26.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (Aug 3): revenue +15% q/q, non-GAAP EPS beat by ~10%, yet the stock fell 11.2% as margins and dilution disappointed (https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/semiconductors/nasdaq-ichr/ichor-holdings/news/ichor-holdings-ichr-stock-sinks-as-margin-recovery-fails-to). Feb 2026 (Q4 2025 print plus raised outlook): +32.7%. A revenue beat alone has not been paid this year.
findings.why_not_priced: Ichor has fallen about 40% since early October, while consensus still sits exactly on the guide midpoint ($330.2m) and the whisper equals consensus. If the market had priced a customer growing 22% q/q into Ichor's quarter, the whisper would sit above consensus and the stock would not be near its post-earnings low. Ichor has not spoken since Aug 3, so Lam's print is newer than the guide.
findings.independence: UCT, a peer selling to the same two customers, beat the top of its Q3 guide (+18% q/q, next finding; different document). Applied Materials guided semi-systems +12% q/q for Aug-Oct (https://247wallst.com/cards/applied-materials-q3-2026-earnings-amat-01kzybvthd5qqamwrtqk59k25x). Lam's customer share comes from Ichor 10-Ks (e.g. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000156459022007613/ichr-10k_20211231.htm). This is a proxy: a subsystem supplier's revenue does not track Lam's quarter one for one.

findings.finding: Ultra Clean (UCT), Ichor's closest listed peer with the same two dominant customers, reported Q3 2026 on Oct 27. Revenue was a record $759.0m, +18% q/q, above the top of its $700-750m guide, and it guided Q4 to $800-860m (+9% q/q at the midpoint). That points to both an Ichor Q3 revenue beat and a Q4 guide able to reach the ~$355m implied bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ichor's guidance line has moved the stock the most: +32.7% on the Feb 2026 raised outlook and -11.2% on Q2 2026, when margins and the ramp disappointed. UCT itself traded at $51.48 on Oct 27 and $49.71 (-9.12%) on Oct 30 (https://www.trivano.com/persbericht/770834-770834.html), so the peer's beat-and-raise was not held by the market.
findings.why_not_priced: Ichor traded around $38 on Oct 26 (Earnings Whispers), rose to $43.08 by Oct 29 and gave it back to about $38.30 today, so the peer read-through was briefly priced and then erased in sector selling. Consensus Q3 has not moved off the guide midpoint since UCT reported.
findings.independence: Lam's +22% q/q (previous finding, separate document). Lam's commentary on 2027 WFE and on supply constraints (next findings) shares one Lam document with the first finding but makes a different claim. Caveat: UCT's inventory rose to $723m from $391m in December 2025, so part of its growth is stocking; that applies to Ichor too (its Q2 inventory build was $38.4m).

findings.finding: On Oct 21 Lam put preliminary 2027 WFE at more than $200bn, against a mid-$150bn 2026 (about +30%), and expects about 10 new Tier-1 fabs in 2027. That supports Ichor's August statement that customer visibility extends 'well into 2027'. The stock has derated on doubts about exactly that multi-quarter ramp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026: a raised forward outlook took the stock +32.7%. Since then forward commentary has been sold (Aug -11.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: Lam's own stock fell 11.8% on that same call (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/LRCX/q1-2027/), and Citi said on Oct 23 that the semicap selloff 'could be just the beginning'. The market is pricing AI-capex doubt, not the customer's 2027 number. If the 2027 outlook were priced, Ichor would not trade at 66% below its high with 10.5% bullish sentiment.
findings.independence: Ichor's own Q2 release says customer visibility reaches 'well into 2027' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652535/000165253526000066/ex-991_26q2xearnings.htm). This finding shares the Lam call with the supply-constraint finding below, which makes a different claim.

findings.finding: Lam guided its December quarter to only $8.6bn (+4.6% q/q) and said it would have been higher without component supply and clean-room constraints, with China revenue 'significantly lower'. Ichor needs about $355m in Q4 (+8% q/q off $330m) to meet its own FY >=30% commitment, and it flagged a late-Q2 parts shortage from a flow-control supplier. Both put the Q4 guide and margins at risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: margins and the ramp disappointed and the stock fell 11.2%. 2025: guide-related misses gave -31.4% (Nov 2025), -30.2% (Aug 2025) and -23.2% (May 2025), all in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Earnings Whispers names the flow-control supplier as the 'obvious risk' (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ICHR/21402). But consensus has not moved and nobody has tied Lam's +4.6% December quarter to Ichor's ~$355m implied Q4. Subsystem shipments lead tool revenue, so Lam's slower December quarter could show up in Ichor's Q4 guide.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers on Ichor's flow-control supplier and its Q2 slip (separate source). UCT's +9% q/q Q4 guide (above) cuts against this finding, so it is sized net of that. This finding shares the Lam call with the 2027 WFE finding above.

findings.finding: Applied Materials, Ichor's second-largest customer (~25-35% of sales in past 10-Ks), guided FQ4 2026 (Aug-Oct) semiconductor-systems revenue to about $7.9bn, +12% q/q from $7.04bn, in line with Ichor's guided +12% midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As for the Lam finding: revenue beats were sold in Q2 2026 (-11.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it predates Ichor's own guide window and agrees with it. It is filed as a non-contradiction of the Q3 read: the second customer is not offsetting Lam.
findings.independence: Secondary source, not Applied's own release. Consistent with Lam and UCT above.

findings.finding: Ichor's Q2 release says the late-quarter parts shortage pushed some Q2 revenue into Q3, after Q2 missed the roughly $300m consensus at $294.8m. That slipped revenue is in the Q3 number, but it already sits inside the $315-345m guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: it lands inside the company's guide. It is filed because it lowers the risk of a miss on the reported quarter.
findings.independence: Ichor's Q2 release says extra growth planned for Q2 is realised in Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652535/000165253526000066/ex-991_26q2xearnings.htm).

findings.finding: The CFO, COO and a director sold shares after the Q2 print (Form 144s on Aug 18-19, Sep 1, Sep 8, Sep 15 and Oct 2; Form 4s through Oct 5). The sales are reported as under pre-arranged plans, and the last one came about four weeks before the quarter's results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction to insider sales on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Visible on EDGAR and in aggregator feeds (https://quantisnow.com/insight/ichor-holdings-filed-sec-form-8-k-leadership-update-regulation-fd-6256593), so mostly priced. Filed small because it bears on management's conviction in the H2 ramp.
findings.independence: None. The plan-based nature weakens it.

findings.finding: October's semicap tape is a reaction function that sells beats. The SOX fell eight sessions in a row through Oct 16 (the longest streak since 2008), Citi warned on Oct 23 that the semicap selloff 'could be just the beginning', Lam fell 11.8% on a record quarter, and UCT fell 9.1% on Oct 30 three days after a beat-and-raise. A good Ichor print enters the same tape.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Lam -11.8% after its record Sep quarter (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/LRCX/q1-2027/). UCT -9.12% on Oct 30 (https://www.trivano.com/persbericht/770834-770834.html). Ichor itself fell 11.2% on a Q2 EPS beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The selling itself is in the price (-39.5% in 20 days). What may be unpriced is that a beat on the reported quarter will not be enough; that is a statement about the reaction, not the number.
findings.independence: Citi via Barron's/Pluang, 2026-10-23 (https://pluang.com/en/news-feed/masalah-saham-peralatan-chip-baru-mulai). Partly offset by the washed-out positioning in the next finding.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out. The stock is -39.5% over 20 days, 66% below its 52-week high and below the $80.70 ATM price, with Earnings Whispers bullish sentiment at 10.5% (from 28.4%). Short interest is 7.1% of shares outstanding at 3.5 days to cover (Oct 15), so a print that holds the H2 ramp meets a low bar and some shorts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From a depressed base in Feb 2026, a held or raised outlook gave +32.7%. From an elevated base in Aug 2026, an EPS beat gave -11.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: The low expectations themselves are priced. What remains is asymmetry: with the whisper at consensus and the stock at its post-earnings low, the bar is a held ramp, not a raise. The skew (+1.09) is balanced, not bearish.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers sentiment and price data (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ICHR/21402).

findings.finding: Financing: the Q2 ATM raised $195.4m net at an average $80.70, lifting cash to $256.5m against about $120.6m of debt. The money funds a corroborated ramp (inventory +$38.4m, Malaysia high-volume site, internal-content capex), so another raise into this print is unlikely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ATM disclosure on the Q2 print came with -11.2%, read as dilution (Simply Wall St 2026-08-04).
findings.why_not_priced: Known. Filed small because the balance sheet takes overhang risk off the guide: negative operating cash flow until H1 2027 is funded.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers on cash burn and the operating cash flow timing.

outside_window.finding: Applied Materials reports its FQ4 2026 in mid-November, after the exit window. That is the next customer read on the Q4 ramp.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR 8-Ks since 2026-08-03: none, so no pre-announcement, guidance update or leadership change in the window

baseline_tension: The customer and peer evidence leans positive against a balanced skew and a -39.5% run-up, so it cuts against the run-up. But the sector's October habit of selling record prints (Lam, UCT) is the same force that made the run-up, which keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Ichor's Q2 EPS beat was sold -11.2% and Lam/UCT record prints were sold, so the Lam read-through goes 1.5 -> 1.0, UCT 1.2 -> 1.0, AMAT 0.3 -> 0.2, and p_up 55 -> 54.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the Q2-to-Q3 slipped revenue is inside the $315-345m guide, 0.3 -> 0.1.

Rule 7 (positioning): short interest of 7.1% / 3.5 days is not crowded, but with the stock -40% the 'beats sold' negative goes -1.5 -> -1.2. The Q4-guide negative is kept at -1.5, already net of UCT's offsetting guide.
Rule 4 (financing): the ATM funds a corroborated ramp, so +0.2 stays.
Rules 5 and 9: the Lam proxy is sized net of AMAT, which grows at the guided rate and does not offset. Left standing.
